summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — WKL.AS +3%, BESI.AS +3%, ZAL.DE +2%, SGE.L +2%, DSFIR.AS +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AAL.L -5%, STLAP.PA -4%, GLEN.L -4%, GLE.PA -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AAL.L (-4.74%) — No confirmed company-specific news found; the move looks like a sector-wide copper/miners selloff on weak copper prices, with possible Teck-merger China approval uncertainty weighing. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: AAL.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap diversified miner, and no strategy's universe includes UK mining names. A sector-driven drift with no discrete catalyst gives a news-reactive bot nothing to trigger on.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Oct 20 news. Likely a continued rebound after JPMorgan raised its target from €87 to €100 (overweight) on Oct 19, when the stock led the AEX, up about 3%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WKL.AS is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam information-services name that no strategy lists. The move was a slow analyst-upgrade rebound with no gap or volume spike, so momentum and news filters would not have fired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AEX/Euronext large caps to the momentum-trader universe, and add an analyst-target-raise trigger (e.g. a target-price raise of ≥10% from a tier-1 broker) as a news-reactive entry signal.
